data.name: Masakin
data.gender_notes: Masakin is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Islamic culture, Masakin refers to the honor and respect given to guests. The term is derived from the Arabic word ‘Sakan’ which means to reside or dwell. Masakin is a reminder of the importance of hospitality and kindness towards others, as our Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) once said, ‘Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honour his guest.’ (Bukhari)
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes welcoming and showing kindness to others.
data.etymology: Masakin belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Guests, visitors.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Masakin total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_arabic.name: مساكين
in_arabic.meaning: مساكين تعني الفقراء أو المحتاجين في الإسلام
in_arabic.long_meaning: مساكين هو جمع مذكر سالم من مسكين، وهو الشخص الفقير المحتاج الذي لا يملك ما يكفيه للعيش. وردت كلمة مساكين في القرآن الكريم في عدة مواضع، منها قول الله تعالى: 'وَيُطْعِمُونَ الطَّعَامَ عَلَى حُبِّهِ مِسْكِينًا وَيَتِيمًا وَأَسِيرًا'. تعتبر كلمة مساكين من الألفاظ ذات الدلالة العميقة في الإسلام، حيث تشير إلى حالة الفقر والاحتياج التي قد يمر بها بعض الناس، وتحث على مساعدتهم ومواساتهم.

in_urdu.name: مساکین
in_urdu.meaning: مساکین کا مطلب ہے فقراء یا احتیاج مند لوگ
in_urdu.long_meaning: مساکین (Masakin) عربی زبان کا ایک لفظ ہے جس کا مطلب ہے فقراء یا احتیاج مند لوگ۔ یہ لفظ قرآن مجید میں بھی استعمال ہوا ہے، جیسے کہ اللہ تعالیٰ کا ارشاد ہے: 'وَيُطْعِمُونَ الطَّعَامَ عَلَى حُبِّهِ مِسْكِينًا وَيَتِيمًا وَأَسِيرًا'۔ اردو میں اس لفظ کا استعمال جنوبی ایشیاء کے مسلم معاشروں میں فقراء اور احتیاج مندوں کی مدد اور مواساة کے سیاق میں ہوتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: मसाकिन
in_hindi.meaning: मसाकिन का अर्थ है गरीब या जरूरतमंद लोग
in_hindi.long_meaning: मसाकिन (Masakin) एक अरबी शब्द है जिसका अर्थ है गरीब या जरूरतमंद लोग। यह शब्द कुरआन में भी प्रयोग हुआ है, जैसे कि अल्लाह का फरमान है: 'وَيُطْعِمُونَ الطَّعَامَ عَلَى حُبِّهِ مِسْكِينًا وَيَتِيمًا وَأَسِيرًا'। भारत में मुस्लिम समुदाय में इस शब्द का प्रयोग गरीबों और जरूरतमंदों की मदद और सांत्वना के संदर्भ में होता है।

in_pashto.name: مساکین
in_pashto.meaning: مساکین د بې وزلو یا اړمنډو خلکو معنی
in_pashto.long_meaning: مساکین (Masakin) د عربي کلمې څخه اخیستل شوی دی چې معنی یې د بې وزلو یا اړمنډو خلکو څخه عبارت دی. دا کلمه په قرآن کريم کې هم استعمال شوې ده، لکه څنګه چې الله تعالی فرمايي: 'وَيُطْعِمُونَ الطَّعَامَ عَلَى حُبِّهِ مِسْكِينًا وَيَتِيمًا وَأَسِيرًا'. په افغانستان کې د پښتنو په دوديزو کړنو کې د مساکینو سره مرسته او مواساة د يوې مهمې ديني او ټولنیزې چارې په توګه ګڼل کیږي.

in_english.name: Masakin
in_english.meaning: Masakin means the poor or those in need
in_english.long_meaning: Masakin is a term derived from Arabic, specifically referring to the poor or those in need. The word 'Masakin' is a plural form of 'Miskin', which appears in the Quran, such as in the verse: 'They give food, in spite of their love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive.' (76:8). In Islamic tradition, Masakin symbolizes compassion and charity towards those less fortunate. Historically, it has been used across Muslim cultures to denote the vulnerable and to encourage support and benevolence towards them.

data.cultural_impact: The concept of Masakin signifies the deep-rooted tradition of hospitality and respect for guests in Islamic culture, emphasizing the importance of extending a warm welcome and providing comfort to those who visit. This was highly valued in ancient Arab societies, particularly in the desert, where the scarcity of resources necessitated a strong social bond and mutual support system.
data.spiritual_significance: Aside from its cultural significance, Masakin holds a special spiritual meaning. According to Islamic teachings, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and his companions were exceptional hosts who showed extraordinary kindness to their guests, seeing them as God’s guests. The Prophet (peace be upon him) once said, "The believer's shade on the Day of Resurrection will be his charity." (Tirmidhi). Through acts of kindness and generosity to guests, Muslim communities create a ripple effect, nurturing a collective spirit of compassion while fostering the belief that every human being holds a valuable place in the eyes of Allah.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Battuta's Travels: Ibn Battuta describes a mosque in Damascus named Masjid al-Masakin, which translates to 'mosque of the poor'. He explains that it is a large mosque with a school and a kitchen (kitchen was used to distribute food to the poor), and that it was built by Damascus' Ayyubid ruler, Al-Malik al-Nasir Salah al-Din Yusuf ibn Ayyub (r. 1230-1260).
historical_references.context: Construction of Masjid al-Masakin in Damascus

historical_references.reference: Al-Maqrizi's The History of the Prophets and Kings of Egypt: Al-Maqrizi recounts that during the Mamluk Sultanate in Egypt, a man named Ibrahim al-Halabi (d. 1365) went around begging and collected alms for building a mosque. The mosque, named Masjid al-Masakin, was completed in 1354 and was located in Cairo. It was known to be a mosque for the poor, and had a special room for housing the poor.
historical_references.context: Construction of Masjid al-Masakin in Cairo

modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Masakin' in the Islamic context refers to the homes or shelters for the needy or the poor. In modern times, this concept has been adapted and implemented through various platforms. On real estate marketplaces like Zillow, Masakin can be seen in the form of initiatives and programs that aim to provide affordable housing for low-income families and individuals. Community platforms like IslamHelp and MuslimGiving facilitate donations and fundraising for building and maintaining Masakins around the world. These platforms allow individuals to contribute to the cause and make a difference in the lives of those in need. Overall, Masakin remains a significant aspect of Islamic social welfare and continues to evolve with the times through innovative and technological solutions.
